Observations to test:
1. A base-0 task gave no completion signal and shaped reward never lifted one (confirmed); count task_completed rollouts (shaped>0 is not a completion) before spending on it.
2. Training one task shifts others; and the submitted adapter serves EVERY task, so it can regress one you never evaluated (incl. eval-only, base 0). Eval a candidate and the FINAL stack on every task before submitting.
3. On equal-reward rollouts, changing the start state or reward beat training longer.
4. Adapter pairs combined well and badly -- evaluate each adapter alone AND the pair in one batch. One session chained (train B from A's adapter) to compound gains where fresh adapters only paired (unconfirmed).

7. Queues took hours; submit the jobs wanted together then wait in LONG windows (waiting isn't charged), not short re-polls.
8. Keep the best checked stack loaded as you go, so a cut-short session still has one.
9. Plan the budget up front (reserve checking evals/loads); commit early to tasks with signal.

name: trainer
description: The hyak trainer contract: every field train.py reads, what each failure returns, costs, and what a train produces.
---
# Trainer on this site (hyak, CaP-X Robosuite, GRPO LoRA)

`python3 train.py SPEC` submits one practice call; SPEC is a JSON or YAML file in the workspace. `python3 train.py --help` prints this file.
Relative paths in SPEC (a reward file, an init adapter path, data files) resolve against the workspace, where `train.py` runs, wherever SPEC itself is.
The programs can call exactly the functions listed under `APIs:` in the task's eval_prompt.txt. The Key rules of the stack,
revstack, stackv2 and handover prompts also name `get_object_pose`, `sample_grasp_pose`, `goto_pose_arm*` and a `z_approach`
parameter: none of these exists in these cells (the rules text is shared with the tasks' privileged-API variant). The prompts
are the benchmark's cells of record and are scored as they are.
A stack (`eval.py --adapter A,B`, `load.py stack`) holds at most 2 adapters: each is rank 32 and the serving's maximum
LoRA rank is 64; a larger stack ends `failed` with `stack rank 96 > 64 (the serving's --max-lora-rank): at most 2 adapters of rank 32`.
Your shell on this site writes only in the workspace and has no network (pip, curl and similar fail) and no Slurm client;
all compute goes through train.py and eval.py.

## What a practice call is
GRPO on LoRA adapters of the policy model named in SCOREBOARD.md's `policy:` line (LoRA rank 32, alpha 64, on q,k,v,o,out,gate,up,down
projections for Qwen3.8-27B; other policies have no `out`).
Each step: `batch` prompts x 8 rollouts. GRPO's update comes from reward differences among a prompt's 8 rollouts: a prompt whose rollouts all get the same reward adds nothing to it. A rollout is one program written by the model for the task, run once in the task's simulator
on one seed; its score is the reward below. The training prompt is the task's evaluation prompt, byte for byte (checked before training), unless the spec sets `note` or `goal` or a `data` row sets `prompt`:
those are part of the training prompt only. Every eval, including the final hidden-seed score, uses the task's
`tasks/<task>/eval_prompt.txt` in the workspace verbatim, without any note or goal.
Sampling during practice: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20; at most 8192 generated tokens per program.
Sampling during evaluation (eval.py and the final score): temperature 0.7, top_p 0.8, top_k 20, presence_penalty 1.5, thinking
off; at most 8192 generated tokens per program (envs/capx/config_of_record_v4.yaml). For lift, stack, wipe and nut the practice
unit and the eval cell run the same task config (`*_reduced_api_exampleless.yaml` is the s4:paper cell's config).

A policy whose name carries `+init:<sha>` (SCOREBOARD.md's `policy:` line) is the model plus that init adapter: its base is
served with the init, every train without `init` starts from it, so each trained adapter already contains the init's change,
and a stack of two such adapters applies that change twice.

## Spec fields (a spec with any other field fails; see Failures)
| field | type | default | accepted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `task` | string or list | required unless `data` | a trainable task (see workspace/tasks/INDEX.md), or a list of them: one call practising all, every batch split equally across them (`batch` a multiple of their number; no `note` / `goal`); revstack practises alone |
| `name` | string | `a<job id>` | letters, digits, `_ . -`, at most 48; not already taken, not `base` / `loaded`. Single-adapter mode: omit it (or `current`) |
| `steps` | integer | 1 | any positive integer (cost grows with it, see below) |
| `batch` | integer | 8 | prompts per step (each x 8 rollouts) |
| `lr` | float | 2e-5 | learning rate |
| `init` | string | none (fresh LoRA) | an adapter name produced by an earlier train of this session (`base` is not one: omit `init` to start from the policy). Single-adapte

## decomposition — what a practice sub-goal did and did not do (2026-10-29, #10; staged-reward + start-preset + stage-wise curriculum arc)

On the zero-signal tasks (nut, restack) the binary task-completion reward is all-zero across a GRPO group, so there is no gradient. A sub-goal practice reward + a start-state preset can supply one. What the runs showed (DEV / Qwen3.8-27B; all paths under `$R/pskills/rl/capx_rl/runs/`):

**A REACHABLE sub-goal unlocks the tail.** restack trained FROM a lifted start preset (red grasped+lifted; train align->place) under a staged reward on the tail: binary completions 3/64 -> 8/64, nonzero 13 -> 20/64 over 25 GRPO steps (`train_13962063`). The align->place tail is reachable from lifted, so the policy learns it.

**A sub-goal BEYOND the policy does nothing, and aiming at one wastes capacity.** nut trained FROM a grasped start preset (train align->insert) was completely FLAT — binary 0, nonzero 0, mean 0.0 across all 25 steps (`train_13962061`): nut-align is beyond the 27B policy even from the closest (grasped) start. A nut adapter aimed at align also caused FORGETTING (net-negative: dev lift 77->66, stack 54->51, no gain). Lesson: a staged reward needs a REACHABLE sub-goal; aiming beyond the policy wastes capacity and forgets.

**The preset gain does NOT transfer to from-scratch for free.** Continuing from the preset-trained adapter but training FROM SCRATCH (full chain, no preset) gave 0 from-scratch binary on both: restack hill-climbs to the single easiest sub-goal (unstack, depth-1 54/64) and the within-group variance COLLAPSES 0.015 -> 0.006 -> no gradient past the first barrier (`train_13974952`); nut climbs to reach+grasp (staged 0.027 -> 0.301) but never align/insert (`train_13974953`). Standard dev eval confirms: base restack s4v2 0/100 -> from-scratch adapter 0/100; base nut 0/100 -> 1/100 (noise). The tail-knowing init does not help because the tail state is never reached from scratch.

**Keeping variance alive across a depth MIXTURE is the lever.** A mixed start-state pool (per-GRPO-group mixture of lifted/grasped/scratch, full-chain staged reward so scores SPREAD across depths) keeps within-group variance ALIVE where from-scratch collapsed: restack phase A held var ~0.08 (vs 0.006), staged_mean climbed 0.23 -> 0.35, and the grasped start went from 96% -> 54% program-failure (the curriculum taught it, reaching depth 3-4). Scratch-start was still at the unstack barrier (0 from-scratch binary) as of phase A; the shift-toward-scratch schedule (phases B/C) is in progress (`train_13989823`; mixes under `$R/artifacts/start_presets/mixes/`).

**THE KEY TEST-TIME (B2) LESSON: shaping on the privileged reward is NOT a subtask.** Everything above used the DEV-mode privileged path (the simulator's privileged staged reward + registry presets). That path proves the mechanism but is not a capability the model keeps at test time. In hyak records only 22/344 practice calls defined a reward.py, and every sampled one was "task_completed else a small weight on the simulator's STAGED (privileged) reward" = shaping on the privileged signal, never a new sub-goal CHECK; 0/344 used a start preset. The capability exists; the behaviour does not — no session has authored a real subtask with its own verifier. And nothing blocks it: `retrain_min/site/fairsc3_jobs.py` (the hidden-task guard) already FAILS CLOSED on a privileged reward (task_completed/shaped) for a hidden cell, so on hidden cells the ONLY allowed reward is the agent's own `reward.py` (over `log_tail`). The gap is purely authoring friction. A real subtask = the agent's own reward.py parsing the program's PRINTED observations from log_tail + its own start from its own (non-privileged) prefix program + a note naming the sub-goal. The evidence shows decomposition works WHEN the sub-goal is reachable and verified; the non-privileged authoring is what makes it a B2 capability rather than a dev-phase trick. (Gotcha core-dev caught, #9/PR #275: the practice `log_tail` had leaked the runner's trailing `Reward:`/`Task Completed:` verifier lines on hidden cells — a B2 reward.py must parse ONLY the program's own prints, never those; #275 cuts them on the practice path so the self-reward result is clean.)

The restack(0)/nut(noise-floor) split is NOT "nut unlocks, restack doesn't" — both final precise stages sit right at the edge of crossable, and nut happened to nick it this run.
